messages:
maria: Heads up — I opened a TF PR that changes the gpupool module to support tiered capacity (min_gpus_per_node + max_gpus_per_node) and renames variable `gpu_count` -> `gpus_per_node`. Default changed from 4 -> 2 which means modules relying on the old default will see a planned shrink. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842 :warning:

kevin: Which environments would be impacted if this lands as-is? production only? any spot/reserved mix differences?

maria: Impacted where we didn't explicitly set gpus_per_node — most app staging stacks, and some prod regional pools in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Notably, clusters that used the old implicit default of 4 will plan to drop to 2. Spot vs reserved: the module also toggles spot fallback behavior based on sizing rules, so smaller counts change bin-packing and could increase spot churn.

ajay: Oof. We should avoid a breaking default change in a minor. Options: revert default and introduce a migration, or add compat shim (accept old var name as alias) + explicit migration step. Also consider adding a CI plan guard that rejects size changes to IGMs unless approved.

maria: I added an alias var and a deprecation note in the PR but there are still a bunch of stacks that don't set any value. Plan output shows 3 regional IGMs with size "4 -> 2". I don't want a global apply to go live without a canary.

sam: Can we do a staged rollout? ops-runner-bot can apply to a single region via the gitops staging channel, then wait 24h for telemetry.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary apply requested by @maria for env=prod-us-west-2 at 2026-03-20T14:30Z. Please confirm with :thumbsup:.

kevin: From a cost viewpoint shrinking reduces steady-state spend but risks increased latency if throughput isn't sufficient. Also watch OOM/retry rates. We should run perf/load test against a canary cluster before switching more regions.

ajay: Proposed rollout plan:
1) Revert the new default in module (safe minor) and merge alias/deprecation commit.
2) Add a GH Actions plan-guard job that fails if terraform show -json indicates instance group "size" updates for addresses matching gpupool igms (unless PR is labeled gpupool-rollout).
3) Create a small terraform state update/migration script to explicitly set gpus_per_node to old default where missing (so future merges are no-op).
4) Do a targeted gitops apply to staging, run perf checks, then canary in us-west-2, then roll region-by-region.

maria: I'll push a follow-up commit restoring the 4 default and include the migration script + README steps. Draft of the plan-guard snippet I put in the PR description:

```
# fail CI if any gpupool IGM size would be updated
terraform plan -out=tfplan.binary
terraform show -json tfplan.binary | jq -r '.resource_changes[] | select(.address | test("module\\..*gpupool.*google_compute_region_instance_group_manager")) | select(.change.actions | index("update")) | select(.change.before.size != .change.after.size) | .address' | ifne exit 1
```

sam: Nice. Also add a label-based override so infra leads can approve legitimate size changes (label = gpupool-rollout).

kevin: Agree. Also add a short post-apply checklist to track latency, GPU utilization, OOMs, and spot preemptions for 48h. We should block wider rollout if any of those cross thresholds.

maria: Will do. I'm creating per-region migration PRs to set explicit gpus_per_node in the env overlays so the main module change becomes a no-op. Not merging the module PR until those land. tagging @kevin @ajay for the canary window. :thumbsup:

ajay: One more safety: add lifecycle = { ignore_changes = ["target_size"] } to the IGM resource in the module as a temporary last-resort gate so accidental applies don't shrink pools. We'll document removing it post-migration.

maria: Good call. I'll add that as a temporary commit that we plan to remove after migration.

kevin: Thanks — keep us posted.

maria: Will update PR and post links here when the per-region PRs are up.
